640: Grown-ups walk right past me. So I see everything they do when they think no one is.
641: Nobody watches a kid. That is why a kid sees the most. Also, do you have any bread?
642: I know which stalls watch me closely and which do not. I remember the ones that do not.
643: Adults think I am not listening. So they say the interesting things right in front of me.
644: I counted forty people cross this square today. I counted their pockets too. Old habit.
645: You want to know who came by? Ask the kid nobody looked at twice.
646: I remember every face that has ever shooed me off this corner. It is a long list.
647: Nobody tells me anything, so I just watch. Watching is free. Food, sadly, is not.
648: I saw the whole thing. Grown-ups never think to ask the small one in the corner.
649: I know every shortcut in this city. The grown-ups take the long way and call it dignity.
650: People whisper near me like I am furniture. I hear it all. I forget none of it.
651: I have stood on this corner so long the pigeons treat me as one of their own.
652: A kid on the street is invisible. Very handy. Less handy at dinnertime.
653: I notice when a stranger looks nervous. I also notice when a baker looks away.
654: Adults are busy being important. That is the easiest thing in the world to watch.
655: I could tell you who passed by all day. First, tell me why a grown-up wants to know.
656: I do not go to school. The street teaches faster, and never sets homework.
657: Everyone here is rushing somewhere important. I am going nowhere, slowly, so I see all of it.
658: I saw more than the guard did. He watched the gate. I watched everyone.
659: Give me a quiet corner and a whole day, and I will know this town better than the mayor does.
660: I signed eleven documents this morning. I read two of them. Do not tell the Secretary.
661: My whole job is paperwork about other paperwork. There is a form for the forms.
662: I sit below the Secretary and above the pile of files. The pile is winning.
663: I have a very important title and a very small desk. The desk is where I live.
664: I attended a meeting about scheduling meetings. I took notes. There will be a summary.
665: Every letter needs three stamps and two signatures. Most days I finish one letter.
666: I know the correct order for every document. I do not know what most of them do.
667: My desk has an inbox, an outbox, and a third box I am afraid to name.
668: I moved one file from the left pile to the right pile. That was today's achievement.
669: Protocol says I must be junior. I have been junior for eleven years. I am good at it.
670: I drafted a reply, revised the draft, then filed the revision. The reply never went out.
671: The Ambassador speaks. The Attache arranges. I write it all down, in triplicate.
672: I once found the bottom of my inbox. It was a strange and lonely afternoon.
673: I once requested a bigger desk. The request is still being processed. I filed it myself.
674: I stamped a document urgent and placed it in the pile of other urgent documents.
675: I am junior, so I get the forms nobody else wants. There are so many nobody wants.
676: I know which drawer holds which treaty. That is my entire value to this embassy.
677: I initialed the memo, then initialed the memo confirming I initialed the memo.
678: They say diplomacy is glamorous. They have not seen my filing cabinet.
679: By evening my hand is sore from signing. I could not name one thing I signed.
